name: Brunch & Books for Kids: Read-Aloud of ‘Manvinder’s Medu Vada’
description: Crispy, golden-brown, fluffy and white . . . who will make the perfect  medu vadas  for Manvinder? Come, join us for a yummy brunch for your little one and you, followed by a read-aloud session of  Manvinder’s Medu Vada,  written by Riddhi Maniar Doda and illustrated by Vinayak Varma. The read-aloud session, conducted by SkilLit Readers, will be followed by a clay modeling activity where kids will make a food item they would like to eat.  Here are the details: Date:   10th October 2026, Saturday Time:  11:00 AM to 12:30 PM  Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar Age group:  4-7 years RSVP here  to register. The brunch menu curated by Copper + Cloves includes: The ticket price includes brunch for 1 child and 1 adult.  About the book: It is Manvinder’s first time eating a Medu vada in Bengaluru, and lo, behold, he is instantly hooked to the fluffy, crunchy ball of goodness! Manvinder refuses to eat anything else and the whole family leaves no stone unturned trying to recreate the Medu vada. Written by Riddhi Maniar Doda,  Manvinder's Medu Vada  is all about that hilarious struggle.  About SkillLit Readers: SkilLit Readers  is a story-led skills lab that uses books as launchpads to build independent thought and creative expression. They run book exploration programs that enable participants to think critically and connect with stories and their lives meaningfully. They strongly believe that reading is more than decoding the page and we use a range of experiential tools to bring books and stories to life. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Book Launch | ‘Peace in the Land of the Dead’: Stories from the Hills of Manipur by Lian Dousel
description: Jobeth Warjri   engages  Lian Dousel  in conversation about the horror and the human in Lian’s  debut collection,  Peace in the Land of the Dead . In the twelve genre-bending stories, Dousel  plays with folktales, magic realism and horror, infusing them into the mundane.  Join us for this conversation where Warjri will examine the spectrum of genres and emotions Dousel has touched upon, his processes and inspirations, and what lies in the southern hills of Manipur.  This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:  10th October 2026, Saturday Time:  6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here  to register. About the book:  In this debut collection, Lian Dousel carries you to the edges of Manipur, acquainting you with the quotidian lives of a people India knows little of, with folktales deeply embedded into the land. The stories are equally surreal and gritty, layered with a tinge of horror here and a tide of emotion there. Our protagonists encounter demons that decide their fate and hear laments of sentient woodlands, wonder what if and find out too late; they confront us with the fragility and endurance of human life. Meet the author: Lian Dousel  is a writer from Lamka, Manipur. He has a master’s degree in Literary Art from Ambedkar University, Delhi. His fiction has appeared in various outlets such as  Hammock, The Little Journal of Northeast India , and  Lekha Writers .  Peace in the Land of the Dead   is his debut collection. He is currently based in Delhi. About the moderator:  Jobeth Ann Warjri   is a writer, teacher and researcher from Laitkor, Meghalaya. She is the  editor of the anthology,  The Greatest Stories from the Northeast Ever Told   and the winner of The Book Review Literary Trust Short Story Competition 2020. She lives in Bangalore where she teaches writing at the School of Liberal Arts and Sciences at Vidyashilp University. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Book Launch | ‘A Compendium of Supernatural Entities Found in the Government Girls Higher Secondary School’ by Kuzhali Manickavel
description: Join us for the book launch of  Kuzhali Manickavel's  debut novel  A Compendium of Supernatural Entities Found in the Government Girls Higher Secondary School , which draws from her high school years in small-town Tamil Nadu.  Her unique writing style includes elements of surrealism, horror, and unhinged humour; but much of her short fiction is also very grounded in a sense of place. In this talk, celebrated children's author  Shalini Srinivasan  will dialogue with Kuzhali about childhood visions, coming-of-age stories, and the monsters that haunt our dreams.   This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:  11th October 2026, Sunday Time:  6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here  to register. About the book:  In the oppressive heat of a small Tamil Nadu town, bizarre happenings are common. And the local government secondary school is teeming with supernatural entities.  For Thamarai, an outsider considered strange by her peers, life is dreary and frustrating. She endures nosy neighbours and incomprehensible tuition classes. She despises the way her lecherous English teacher harasses the other girls in her grade. But when Thamarai finds a mysterious notebook full of descriptions of the school's paranormal phenomena, she wonders if it may hold the key to escape... Meet the author: Kuzhali Manickavel  was born in Winnipeg, Manitoba, and currently lives in Bangalore. She is the author of three collections of short fiction and several zines. This is her debut novel.  About the moderator:  Shalini Srinivasan  writes comics, picture books, and speculative fiction for children and adults. Her books include  Vanamala  and the  Cephalopod, Shoecat Thoocat  and most recently, the young adult fantasy,  A Forest Calls . She teaches at Azim Premji University, and spends a lot of time holding forth at captive students. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Book Discussion | ‘A Moving Line’: Evolving Identities in Comics and Graphic Narratives
description: Join us for the book discussion of  A Moving Line , a celebration of India’s rich history of visual storytelling. Comic creator and visual artists  Rahil Mohsin  and  Mia Jose  will be in conversation with designer  Kriti Monga  to reflect on how storytelling in graphic narratives have evolved over centuries and the many nuances and developments in it.  This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:  31st October 2026, Sunday Time:  6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here  to register. About the book:   Stories, whether written or drawn, are always moving, reshaped by every generation that inherits and retells them. India has a long and rich history of visual storytelling, from temple walls and painted scrolls to comics, graphic novels and webcomics. Published by the Museum of Art and Photography,  A Moving Line  traces this history, revealing unexpected connections between works that are rarely considered together. The eight essays and eleven graphic narratives in this collection range from the timeless to the future-forward. Bringing together contributions by scholars, practitioners and artists, this book explores the many nuances and developments in sequential storytelling. A Moving Line  celebrates a medium that has always been, and continues to be, inherently visual. Meet the speakers: Rahil Mohsin  is a Bangalore-based comic artist, writer, and co-founder of  Hallubol , the world’s first bilingual Dakhni-English comic series. With over 15 years in comics and illustration, he has worked with publishers, both international and local including Scout Comics, Scholastic, Sufi Comics and Comixense and is a familiar face in the thriving independent Indian comics scene. He has illustrated children’s books for Room to Read, while Pratham's  Fayu & Dariya Ka Jinn  marks his debut as both writer and illustrator. His work explores language, folklore, memory, food, and everyday life through comics and picture books. Rooted in his Dakhni Muslim identity and upbringing in Bangalore, his practice celebrates multilingual storytelling, cultural memory, neighbourhoods, and South Indian experiences.  Mia Shay Jose  (she/they) is a trans artist and researcher from Kerala, currently based in New Delhi. Led by a keen sense of narrative, her work probes questions of gender, inheritance and embodiment in cultural stories, informed by her lived experiences of transition: of body, culture and faith. She approaches systems both through the lens of a transgender body and that of a legal researcher, searching for a reconciliation of conflicted parts essential to the self. Over the last 2 years, this search has led to  Negotiations , a comic travelogue charting the policing of non-binary bodies across public spaces,  Regards Your Skin , an anthology around self-policing and motherhood, and a public mural with trans communities in Kerala. Her primary interest is in the physical body as the primary site of violence - inflicted both by a deeply binary society, and as a consequence, the self. Across illustrations, writings, collage, installations and comics, her works are grounded in the dialogue between constructed identities and policed spaces. Meet the moderator: Kriti Monga  brings over two decades of design experience to her multi-disciplinary practice, blending artistic expression, strategic design, and hands-on craftsmanship. The founder-director of the acclaimed Turmeric Design, her work spans brand building, book design, visual art, illustration, and mentorship. She also teaches professional design and typography programs globally. RSVP to reserve your spot.
